l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: rich man (the rich person) is filled with good things (when he rests)
q: When he rests, he is filled with his good things.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: rich man (the rich person) is blessed (if found blameless and not going after gold)
q: Blessed is the rich person who is found blameless, and who doesn’t go after gold.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: greed at table is a wicked thing (greedy eye)
q: Remember that a greedy eye is a wicked thing.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: greed at table causes being hated (when eating greedily)
q: Don’t eat greedily, lest you be hated.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: greed at table causes wakefulness, colic and griping (in an insatiable man)
q: The pain of wakefulness, colic, and griping are with an insatiable man.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: table manners and moderate eating produces healthy sleep
q: Healthy sleep comes from moderate eating.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is a Maker
q: For these things bless your Maker, who gives you to drink freely of his good things.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the law fills one who seeks it
q: He who seeks the law shall be filled with it, but the hypocrite will stumble at it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: hypocrite stumbles at the law
q: but the hypocrite will stumble at it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who fear the Lord receives discipline
q: He who fears the Lord will receive discipline.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who fear the Lord finds true judgment
q: Those who fear the Lord will find true judgment, and will kindle righteous acts like a light.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who fear the Lord kindles righteous acts (like a light)
q: will kindle righteous acts like a light.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord gives good things (to drink freely)
q: bless your Maker, who gives you to drink freely of his good things.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: feast ruler should be as one of the guests (not lifted up)
q: Don’t be lifted up. Be among them as one of them.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: feast ruler should take care of banquet guests (first, before sitting down)
q: Take care of them first, and then sit down.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: feast ruler receives wreath (for good service)
q: take your place, that you may be gladdened on their account, and receive a wreath for your good service.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: older speaker has right to speak (with sound knowledge, without interrupting the music)
q: Speak, you who are older, for it’s your right, but with sound knowledge; and don’t interrupt the music.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: young man speaks no more than twice (only if asked)
q: Speak, young man, if you are obliged to, but no more than twice, and only if asked.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: music compared to ruby signet in gold (at a wine banquet)
q: As a ruby signet in a setting of gold, so is a music concert at a wine banquet.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: music compared to emerald signet in gold (with pleasant wine)
q: As an emerald signet in a work of gold, so is musical melody with pleasant wine.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord delivers men (those who fear him, in trials)
q: No evil will happen to him who fears the Lord, but in trials once and again he will deliver him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: men originate from ground
q: And all men are from the ground.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: men are in hand of the Lord (like clay of the potter)
q: As the clay of the potter in his hand, all his ways are according to his good pleasure, so men are in the hand of him who made them, to give to them according to his judgment.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord makes different men (ways differ; some blessed, some cursed)
q: In the abundance of his knowledge the Lord distinguished them, and made their ways different.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: opposites in pairs describes works of the Most High (come in pairs, one against another)
q: Look upon all the works of the Most High like this, they come in pairs, one against another.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: opposites in pairs includes sinner opposite of the godly
q: so the sinner is the opposite of the godly.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the law is trusted by wise man (man of understanding)
q: A man of understanding will put his trust in the law. And the law is faithful to him, as when one asks a divine oracle.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: servant is allotted bread, discipline, and work
q: Bread, discipline, and work are for a servant.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: servant seeks liberty (if left idle)
q: Leave his hands idle, and he will seek liberty.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: slave owner should set to work servant (to gain rest and prevent idleness)
q: Set your slave to work, and you will find rest.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: slave owner should treat like himself servant (because bought with blood)
q: If you have a slave, treat him like yourself, because you have bought him with blood.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: slave owner needs servant (like his own soul)
q: For like your own soul, you will need him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the law is faithful (to the man of understanding)
q: And the law is faithful to him, as when one asks a divine oracle.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord distinguishes days (by his knowledge)
q: They were distinguished by the Lord’s knowledge, and he varied seasons and feasts.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord varies seasons and feasts
q: he varied seasons and feasts.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: dreams is a vain thing
q: Divinations, and soothsayings, and dreams, are vain.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who love the Lord has state will live
q: The spirit of those who fear the Lord will live, for their hope is in him who saves them.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who love the Lord has disposition unafraid
q: Whoever fears the Lord won’t be afraid, and won’t be a coward, for he is his hope.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who love the Lord is blessed
q: Blessed is the soul of him who fears the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wrongful sacrifices is a mockery
q: He who sacrifices a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is made in mockery.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wrongful sacrifices is not acceptable (to the Lord)
q: The mockeries of wicked men are not acceptable.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wrongful sacrifices does not pacify sins (regardless of multitude)
q: Neither is he pacified for sins by the multitude of sacrifices.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wrongful sacrifices is compared to killing a son before his father's eyes (when from the goods of the poor)
q: Like one who kills a son before his father’s eyes is he who brings a sacrifice from the goods of the poor.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: dreams gives wings to fools
q: Dreams give wings to fools.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wisdom is complete in faithful mouth
q: Wisdom is complete in a faithful mouth.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: dreams leads astray many
q: For dreams have led many astray.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: dreams is a reflection (vision of dreams)
q: The vision of dreams is a reflection, the likeness of a face near a face.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord watches over those who love him (mighty protection and strong support)
q: The eyes of the Lord are on those who love him, a mighty protection and strong support, a cover from the hot blast, a shade from the noonday sun, a guard from stumbling, and a help from falling.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord gives health, life, and blessing
q: He raises up the soul, and enlightens the eyes. He gives health, life, and blessing.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is hope of those who love the Lord
q: The spirit of those who fear the Lord will live, for their hope is in him who saves them.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord has no pleasure in wrongful sacrifices (offerings of the ungodly)
q: The Most High has no pleasure in the offerings of the ungodly,

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is a judge
q: For the Lord is the judge, and with him is no respect of persons.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord will judge cause of his people
q: until he has judged the cause of his people, and he will make them rejoice in his mercy.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord will make rejoice his people (in his mercy)
q: until he has judged the cause of his people, and he will make them rejoice in his mercy.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: righteous man has sacrifice that is acceptable (will not be forgotten)
q: The sacrifice of a righteous man is acceptable. It won’t be forgotten.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: offerings and sacrifices is commanded by the law
q: For all these things are done because of the commandment.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: offerings and sacrifices enriches altar (offering of the righteous)
q: The offering of the righteous enriches the altar.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: offerings and sacrifices has quality sweet fragrance before the Most High (offering of the righteous)
q: The sweet fragrance of it is before the Most High.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: offerings and sacrifices must not be unrighteous (the Lord is judge)
q: Don’t set your mind on an unrighteous sacrifice, For the Lord is the judge, and with him is no respect of persons.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fatherless and widow has cry against unmerciful and unrighteous (the one who caused the widow's tears)
q: Isn’t her cry against him who has caused them to fall?

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: divine judgment renders to each according to deeds (also according to plans)
q: until he has rendered to every man according to his deeds, and repaid the works of men according to their plans,

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: divine judgment is executed on heathen (vengeance until the arrogant are removed)
q: He will repay vengeance to the heathen until he has taken away the multitude of the arrogant and broken in pieces the sceptres of the unrighteous,

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord shows partiality none (no respect of persons)
q: For the Lord is the judge, and with him is no respect of persons.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mercy is compared to clouds of rain in drought (welcome in time of affliction)
q: Mercy is as welcome in the time of his affliction, as clouds of rain in the time of drought.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: almsgiving is commanded toward the Lord (glorify the Lord with generosity)
q: Glorify the Lord with generosity.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: almsgiving is equivalent to thank offering (he who gives alms)
q: He who gives alms sacrifices a thank offering.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord repays giver sevenfold (to those who give generously)
q: For the Lord repays, and he will repay you sevenfold.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord refuses bribes (gifts offered to bribe him)
q: Don’t plan to bribe him with gifts, for he will not receive them.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord listens to poor man (the wronged)
q: He won’t accept any person against a poor man. He will listen to the prayer of him who is wronged.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord does not despise supplication of fatherless and widow
q: He will in no way despise the supplication of the fatherless or the widow, when she pours out her tale.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is pleased by departure from wickedness
q: To depart from wickedness pleases the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord accepts humble (their prayer pierces the clouds)
q: The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord will crush unmerciful and unrighteous (will not be slack or patient toward the unmerciful)
q: And the Lord will not be slack, neither will he be patient toward them, until he has crushed the loins of the unmerciful.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord is a God of all
q: Have mercy upon us, O Lord the God of all, and look at us with favor;

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: good wife is a richest treasure for her husband
q: He who gets a wife gets his richest treasure, a help meet for him and a pillar of support.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: good wife is a help meet and pillar of support (for her husband)
q: He who gets a wife gets his richest treasure, a help meet for him and a pillar of support.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: good wife has attribute beauty (cheers the countenance)
q: The beauty of a woman cheers the countenance.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: husband is unlike other men wife with kind and humble tongue (if kindness and humility are on her tongue)
q: If kindness and humility are on her tongue, her husband is not like other sons of men.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord is a eternal God
q: all those who are on the earth will know that you are the Lord, the eternal God.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord has relationship to Israel (likened Israel to a firstborn)
q: upon Israel, whom you likened to a firstborn.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Israel is called by Lord (people called by his name)
q: the people that is called by your name

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord has sanctuary in Jerusalem
q: the city of your sanctuary, Jerusalem, the place of your rest.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Jerusalem is a place of the Lord's rest
q: the city of your sanctuary, Jerusalem, the place of your rest.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Jerusalem is a city of the sanctuary
q: the city of your sanctuary, Jerusalem, the place of your rest.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Israel has part Jacob (tribes of Jacob taken as inheritance)
q: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and take them for your inheritance, as from the beginning.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: adversary and enemy has rulers who say There is no one but ourselves (rulers of the enemies)
q: Crush the heads of the rulers of the enemies who say, “There is no one but ourselves.”

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: friend is a friend in name only (some friends)
q: but there is a friend which is only a friend in name.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: godly man has disposition grieves with you if you fail (in his soul is as your own soul)
q: who in his soul is as your own soul, and who will grieve with you, if you fail.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man instructs his own people
q: A wise man will instruct his own people.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man has trait trustworthy understanding
q: The fruits of his understanding are trustworthy.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man receives blessing (called happy by all who see him)
q: A wise man will be filled with blessing. All those who see him will call him happy.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man inherits confidence among his people
q: The wise man will inherit confidence among his people.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man has name lives forever
q: His name will live forever.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: gluttony causes nausea
q: and gluttony causes nausea.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: gluttony causes death (many have perished because of it)
q: Because of gluttony, many have perished

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: gluttony is related to overeating (overeating brings disease)
q: For overeating brings disease

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: friend has disposition turns against him in affliction (a certain companion who rejoices in a friend's gladness)
q: There is a companion who rejoices in the gladness of a friend, but in time of affliction will be against him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: friend should be remembered (including in one's riches)
q: Don’t forget a friend in your soul. Don’t be unmindful of him in your riches.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: counselor has disposition gives counsel in own interest (some counselors)
q: Every counselor extols counsel, but some give counsel in their own interest.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: counselor has disposition takes counsel for himself (reason for caution)
q: Let your soul beware of a counselor, and know in advance what is his interest (for he will take counsel for himself)

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: counsel is extolled by every counselor
q: Every counselor extols counsel

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: counsel should precede every action
q: Let counsel go before every action.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: counsel has faithfulness most faithful when from one's own heart (counsel of your heart)
q: Make the counsel of your heart stand, for there is no one more faithful to you than it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: godly man is keeper of the commandments
q: But rather be continually with a godly man, whom you know to be a keeper of the commandments

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: physician created by Lord
q: for truly the Lord has created him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord heals sick person (the son addressed) (when he prays)
q: My son, in your sickness don’t be negligent, but pray to the Lord, and he will heal you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sick person (the son addressed) is instructed to pray to the Lord (in sickness)
q: My son, in your sickness don’t be negligent, but pray to the Lord, and he will heal you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sick person (the son addressed) needs physician (should not let him leave)
q: Then give place to the physician, for truly the Lord has created him. Don’t let him leave you, for you need him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mourning duration one day or two (according to the dead's merit)
q: Let your mourning be according to his merit, for one day or two, lest you be spoken evil of

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the dead should receive burial (with due honor)
q: Wind up his body with due honor. Don’t neglect his burial.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the dead has state at rest (remembrance should rest too)
q: When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: scribe acquires wisdom (through the opportunity of leisure)
q: The wisdom of the scribe comes by the opportunity of leisure.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: plowman works with oxen (drives them and is occupied in their labors)
q: who drives oxen and is occupied in their labors, and who mostly talks about bulls?

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: plowman has focus turning furrows (loses sleep feeding heifers)
q: He will set his heart upon turning his furrows. His lack of sleep is to give his heifers their fodder.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: craftsman has trait diligence (works night and day to make great variety)
q: So is every craftsman and master artisan who passes his time by night as by day, those who cut engravings of signets. His diligence is to make great variety.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: physician receives gift from king (healing comes from the Most High)
q: For healing comes from the Most High, and he shall receive a gift from the king.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: smith works with unwrought iron (sits by the anvil)
q: So too is the smith sitting by the anvil and considering the unwrought iron.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: smith has trait perfectionism (sets his heart on perfecting and adorning works)
q: He will set his heart upon perfecting his works. He will be careful to adorn them perfectly.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: potter works with clay (fashions it with his arm)
q: He will fashion the clay with his arm and will bend its strength in front of his feet.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: potter has trait productivity (produces handiwork in quantity)
q: He produces his handiwork in quantity.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: craftsman trusts in their hands (applies to all these workers; each skillful in own work)
q: All these put their trust in their hands. Each becomes skillful in his own work.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: craftsman sustains city (without them no city would be inhabited)
q: Without these no city would be inhabited.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: craftsman maintains fabric of the age (their prayer is in their craft)
q: But they will maintain the fabric of the age. Their prayer is in the handiwork of their craft.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: craftsman is absent from council (not sought in the council of the people)
q: They won’t be sought for in the council of the people.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: physician is admired by great men (due to his skill)
q: The skill of the physician will lift up his head. He will be admired in the sight of great men.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: physician asks blessing from Lord (for success in diagnosis and healing)
q: For they also shall ask the Lord to prosper them in diagnosis and in healing for the maintenance of life.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: physician has role healer (recovery is sometimes in his hands)
q: There is a time when recovery is in their hands.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: medicines created by Lord (made out of the earth)
q: The Lord created medicines out of the earth.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: medicines is not despised by prudent man
q: A prudent man will not despise them.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: medicines function heal and take away pain
q: With them he heals and takes away pain.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord gives skill to men (that he might be glorified in his marvelous works)
q: He gave men skill that he might be glorified in his marvelous works.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (he who meditates in the law) meditates in law of the Most High (applies his soul to it)
q: Not so he who has applied his soul and meditates in the law of the Most High.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: holy children are addressed by speaker
q: Listen to me, you holy children, and bud forth like a rose growing by a brook of water.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: praise of God's creation have quality exceedingly good
q: All the works of the Lord are exceedingly good, and every command will be done in its time.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: praise of God's creation are before the Lord (works of all flesh; cannot be hidden from his eyes)
q: The works of all flesh are before him. It’s impossible to be hidden from his eyes.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord sees everlasting (from everlasting to everlasting)
q: He sees from everlasting to everlasting. There is nothing too wonderful for him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord has property unhindered salvation (no one can hinder it)
q: There is no one who can hinder his salvation.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord makes waters salty waters
q: As he has made the waters salty, so the heathen will inherit his wrath.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord makes ways plain to the godly (his ways are stumbling blocks to the wicked)
q: His ways are plain to the holy. They are stumbling blocks to the wicked.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: necessities of life are for good to the godly (turned into evils for sinners)
q: All these things are for good to the godly, but for sinners, they will be turned into evils.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: necessities of life include water, fire, iron, salt, wheat flour, honey, milk, wine, oil, clothing
q: The main things necessary for the life of man are water, fire, iron, salt, wheat flour, and honey, milk, the blood of the grape, oil, and clothing.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (he who meditates in the law) seeks out wisdom (wisdom of all the ancients)
q: He will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients and will be occupied with prophecies.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: instruments of vengeance obey the Lord (do not disobey his command in their seasons)
q: In their seasons, they won’t disobey his command.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinners and the wicked receive evil things (created from the beginning for sinners)
q: Good things are created from the beginning for the good. So are evil things for sinners.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: praise and prayer is directed to the Lord (holy children told to bless him with songs and harps)
q: Magnify his name and give utterance to his praise with the songs on your lips and with harps!

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (he who meditates in the law) serves among great men
q: He will serve among great men and appear before him who rules.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (he who meditates in the law) travels through foreign nations (because he has learned good and evil among men)
q: He will travel through the land of foreign nations, for he has learned what is good and evil among men.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (he who meditates in the law) was made by the Lord
q: He will apply his heart to return early to the Lord who made him

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (he who meditates in the law) has memory enduring (his name lives from generation to generation)
q: His memory won’t depart. His name will live from generation to generation.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (he who meditates in the law) is declared wise by foreign nations (nations declare his wisdom)
q: Nations will declare his wisdom.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (he who meditates in the law) is praised by congregation
q: The congregation will proclaim his praise.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (he who meditates in the law) glories in law of the Most High (law of the covenant of the Lord)
q: will glory in the law of the covenant of the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sons of Adam bear heavy yoke (from birth until burial)
q: A heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam, from the day of their coming forth from their mother’s womb, until the day for their burial in the mother of all things.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fear of the Lord is better than riches and strength
q: Riches and strength will lift up the heart. The fear of the Lord is better than both.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fear of the Lord lacks nothing (no need to seek help)
q: There is nothing lacking in the fear of the Lord. In it, there is no need to seek help.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fear of the Lord is like garden of blessing (covers a man more than any glory)
q: The fear of the Lord is like a garden of blessing and covers a man more than any glory.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: begging is worse than death (it is better to die than to beg)
q: It is better to die than to beg.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: begging kindles fire in the belly (though sweet in the mouth of the shameless)
q: Begging will be sweet in the mouth of the shameless, but it kindles a fire in his belly.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: things better than both includes praise of God's creation (love of wisdom is better than wine and music)
q: Wine and music rejoice the heart. The love of wisdom is better than both.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: things better than both includes blameless wife (better than children and building a city)
q: A blameless wife is better than both.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: human travail and troubled sleep is created for every man (great travail)
q: Great travail is created for every man.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: human travail and troubled sleep includes fear of death (affects all from throne to burlap)
q: there is wrath, jealousy, trouble, unrest, fear of death, anger, and strife.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: human travail and troubled sleep includes troubled sleep (night sleep changes knowledge, visions trouble the heart)
q: he is troubled in the vision of his heart, as one who has escaped from the front of battle.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: death troubles sons of Adam (expectation of it and the day of death cause fear)
q: The expectation of things to come, and the day of death, trouble their thoughts, and cause fear in their hearts.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinners suffer sevenfold more calamities (compared to all creatures)
q: To all creatures, human and animal, and upon sinners sevenfold more,

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinners cause flood (calamities created for the wicked)
q: All these things were created for the wicked, and because of them the flood came.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: almsgiving endures forever
q: Almsgiving endures forever.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: almsgiving is better than relatives and helpers (rescues in affliction)
q: Relatives and helpers are for a time of affliction, but almsgiving rescues better than both.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom exalts son (the addressee) (her sons)
q: Wisdom exalts her sons, and takes hold of those who seek her.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord hears the poor (the supplication of one cursing in bitterness of soul; he made him)
q: For if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul, he who made him will hear his supplication.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord fights for son (the addressee) (if he strives for the truth to death)
q: Strive for the truth to death, and the Lord God will fight for you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: son (the addressee) is instructed to give promptly to the poor (not delay giving to the needy)
q: Don’t put off giving to him who is in need.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: son (the addressee) is instructed to be a father to the fatherless (will then be as a son of the Most High)
q: Be as a father to the fatherless, and like a husband to their mother. So you will be as a son of the Most High, and he will love you more than your mother does.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the poor is owed generosity to the poor (should not be deprived of living or made to wait)
q: My son, don’t deprive the poor of his living. Don’t make the needy eyes wait long.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: generosity to the poor is commanded by son (the addressee) (don't turn away from one who asks)
q: Don’t turn your eye away from one who asks.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom takes hold of those who seek wisdom
q: Wisdom exalts her sons, and takes hold of those who seek her.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom is loved by the Lord (the Lord loves those who love her)
q: The Lord loves those who love her.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom forsakes those who seek wisdom (if he goes astray, hands him over to his fall)
q: If he goes astray, she will forsake him, and hand him over to his fall.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom disciplines those who seek wisdom (at first walks with him in crooked ways, bringing fear and dread, until she trusts his soul)
q: For at the first she will walk with him in crooked ways, and will bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her judgments.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom is known by speech
q: For wisdom will be known by speech, and instruction by the word of the tongue.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who seek wisdom will be filled with gladness (those who seek her early)
q: Those who seek her early will be filled with gladness.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who seek wisdom minister to the Lord (those who serve her minister to the Holy One)
q: Those who serve her minister to the Holy One.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who seek wisdom is loved by the Lord (those who love wisdom)
q: The Lord loves those who love her.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: death is bitter to man at peace in his possessions (memory of death)
q: O death, how bitter is the memory of you to a man who is at peace in his possessions

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: children of sinners complains of sinners and the ungodly (because of suffered disgrace)
q: Children will complain of an ungodly father, because they suffer disgrace because of him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinners and the ungodly has destiny perdition (going from a curse)
q: so the ungodly will go from a curse to perdition.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinners and the ungodly forsakes law of the Most High
q: Woe to you, ungodly men, who have forsaken the law of the Most High God!

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinners and the ungodly has name fate blotted out (evil name)
q: the evil name of sinners will be blotted out.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: good name continues forever
q: a good name continues forever.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: good name is worth more than thousand great treasures of gold (continues longer)
q: it continues with you longer than a thousand great treasures of gold.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: shame is appropriate for sexual immorality and sexual offenses (before father and mother)
q: Be ashamed of sexual immorality before father and mother

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: shame is appropriate for lying (before prince and mighty man)
q: of a lie before a prince and a mighty man

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: shame is appropriate for offense (before judge and ruler)
q: of an offense before a judge and ruler

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: shame is appropriate for iniquity (before congregation and the people)
q: of iniquity before the congregation and the people

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: death is acceptable to needy man in old age (its sentence)
q: O death, your sentence is acceptable to a man who is needy and who fails in strength, who is in extreme old age

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: shame is appropriate for unjust dealing (before partner and friend)
q: of unjust dealing before a partner and friend

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: shame is appropriate for theft (where you sojourn)
q: and of theft in the place where you sojourn.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: shame is appropriate for revealing secrets
q: of repeating and speaking what you have heard, and of revealing of secrets.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: shame yields favor in sight of every man (when ashamed of the right things)
q: So you will be ashamed of the right things and find favor in the sight of every man.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: death is sentence from the Lord (over all flesh)
q: This is the sentence from the Lord over all flesh.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: death is good pleasure of the Lord
q: why do you refuse when it is the good pleasure of the Most High?

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: children of sinners is abominable
q: The children of sinners are abominable children

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: children of sinners frequents dwellings of the ungodly
q: they frequent the dwellings of the ungodly.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: children of sinners has inheritance fate perish
q: The inheritance of sinners’ children will perish

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: children of sinners has posterity fate perpetual disgrace
q: with their posterity will be a perpetual disgrace.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord knows all knowledge (as the Most High)
q: For the Most High knows all knowledge.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord made works of the Lord (nothing imperfect)
q: He has made nothing imperfect.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: works of the Lord are full of his glory
q: The Lord’s work is full of his glory.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: works of the Lord are in his words
q: The Lord’s works are in his words.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: works of the Lord are desirable
q: How desirable are all his works!

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: works of the Lord are obedient
q: They are all obedient.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: works of the Lord remain forever (in all manner of uses)
q: All these things live and remain forever in all manner of uses.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: works of the Lord exist in pairs (one opposite the other)
q: All things are in pairs, one opposite the other.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: works of the Lord are unchanged by addition or diminishing
q: Nothing has been added to them, nor diminished from them.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the sun looks at all things (gives light)
q: The sun that gives light looks at all things.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: daughter (a father's daughter) is cause of wakefulness to her father (secret cause)
q: A daughter is a secret cause of wakefulness to a father.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord searches out the deep and the heart
q: He searches out the deep and the heart.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: honest business dealings require things handed over by number and weight
q: Whatever you hand over, let it be by number and weight.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: honest business dealings require giving and receiving in writing
q: In giving and receiving, let all be in writing.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: honest business dealings include exactness of scales and weights (not to be ashamed of)
q: of exactness of scales and weights

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord has understanding of secrets of the deep and the heart
q: He has understanding of their secrets.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting
q: He is from everlasting to everlasting.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord needs no counselor
q: He had no need of any counselor.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord declares past and future things
q: He declares the things that are past and the things that shall be, and reveals the traces of hidden things.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord has hidden from him no thought or word
q: No thought escapes him. There is not a word hidden from him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord has not given power to the saints (to declare all his marvelous works)
q: The Lord has not given power to the saints to declare all his marvelous works

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord established the universe (in his glory)
q: which the Almighty Lord firmly settled, that the universe might be established in his glory.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the sun is a marvelous instrument
q: is a marvelous instrument, the work of the Most High.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: moon is a instrument of the army on high
q: an instrument of the army on high, shining in the structure of heaven,

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: rainbow made by the Lord
q: Look at the rainbow, and praise him who made it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: rainbow encircles sky (stretched out by the hands of the Most High)
q: It encircles the sky with its glorious circle. The hands of the Most High have stretched it out.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: snow falls by the Lord (by his commandment)
q: By his commandment, he makes the snow fall

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: snow has attribute dazzling whiteness
q: The eye is dazzled at the beauty of its whiteness.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: snow falls like lighting of locusts
q: It falls down like the lighting of locusts.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: frost is poured by the Lord (on the earth like salt)
q: He also pours out frost on the earth like salt.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the sun made by the Lord
q: Great is the Lord who made it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: clouds are made strong by the Lord (by his mighty power)
q: By his mighty power, he makes the clouds strong

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: lightnings are sent by the Lord (as his judgment)
q: swiftly sends the lightnings of his judgment.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: winds and storms are controlled by the Lord (south wind blows at his will)
q: At his will, the south wind will blow.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sea was calmed by the Lord (by his counsel)
q: By his counsel, he has calmed the deep and planted islands in it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the sun has attribute burning heat (at noon, dries up the land)
q: At noon, it dries up the land. Who can stand against its burning heat?

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sea contains islands (planted by the Lord)
q: By his counsel, he has calmed the deep and planted islands in it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sea contains sea creatures (strange and wondrous works)
q: There are also those strange and wondrous works in it— variety of all that has life and the huge creatures of the sea.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sea has attribute dangers (told by those who sail on it)
q: Those who sail on the sea tell of its dangers.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sky has attribute clear (pride of the heavenly heights)
q: The pride of the heavenly heights is the clear sky, the appearance of heaven, in the spectacle of its glory.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mountains are shaken by the Lord (at his appearing)
q: At his appearing, the mountains will be shaken.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: messengers succeed because of the Lord
q: Because of him, his messengers succeed.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is awesome and exceedingly great
q: The Lord is awesome and exceedingly great!

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the sun has attribute three times hotter than a furnace (compared to a man tending a furnace)
q: A man tending a furnace is in burning heat, but the sun three times more

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is greater than all his works
q: he is himself the greater than all his works.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord made all things
q: For the Lord made all things.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord upholds all things (by his word)
q: By his word, all things hold together.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is unseen no one has seen him
q: Who has seen him, that he may describe him?

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: praise of God's creation is insufficient cannot praise him enough (even with full strength)
q: Don’t be weary, because you can’t praise him enough.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: praise of God's creation is directed to the Lord (exalt him as much as you can)
q: Glorify the Lord and exalt him as much as you can!

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the sun has course hastened by the Lord (at his word)
q: At his word, he hastens on its course.
